articles.title: Sorteo Europa League: camino tortuoso para Real Sociedad y Celta
articles.standfirst: Los equipos españoles ya conocen a sus rivales para la fase de liga de la competición
articles.summary: Los equipos españoles ya conocen a sus rivales para la fase de liga de la competición
articles.body: La fase liga de la UEFA Europa League 2026-27 ya ha sido sorteada, y los dos representantes españoles, Celta de Vigo y Real Sociedad, ya conocen a los ocho rivales a los que se medirán en esta primera fase de la competición. Los vascos partían desde el bombo 1 y los gallegos, desde el bombo 3. El equipo donostiarra que dirige Pellegrino Matarazzo -vuelve a la competición tras ganar la Copa del Rey 2025-26- se medirá a Olympique de Lyon (casa), Juventus (fuera), Viktoria Plzen (casa), Union Saint-Giloise (fuera), Bournemouth (casa), Crystal Palace (fuera), Torrense (casa) y Lillestrom (fuera). Por su parte, el Celta de Claudio Giráldez -repite por segundo curso seguido en la competición tras haber llegado a cuartos en la edición pasada- tendrá que enfrentarse a Juventus (casa), Olympique de Marsella (fuera), Union Saint-Giloise (casa), Celtic de Glasgow (fuera), Bournemouth (casa), Omona (fuera), Lillestrom (casa) y Beer Sheva (fuera). Serán cuatro partidos en casa y otros cuadro a domicilio y ambos equipos de hecho 'comparten' hasta cuatro de sus ocho contendientes, la mitad, para este camino que pretenden culminar con la clasificación hacia la ronda de eliminatorias. La primera jornada de la fase liga de la UEFA Europa League tendrá lugar el miércoles 16 y el jueves 17 de septiembre, coincidiendo con la jornada 6 de LaLiga EA Sports.

articles.title: Trabzonspor: Turkish club reject Fatih Tekke's resignation following Europa League exit
articles.summary: Trabzonspor say Fatih Tekke's decision stems from the "intense emotional impact" of the Europa League exit.
articles.body:
Trabzonspor have rejected the "emotional" resignation of head coach Fatih Tekke after the Turkish side, who signed Mohamed Salah in the summer, were knocked out of the Europa League on Thursday.

The Super Lig team suffered a 4-0 defeat by Ferencvaros in Hungary to lose the play-off tie 5-0 on aggregate.

In the aftermath, Tekke, who led Trabzonspor to a third-place finish in the league last season, tendered his resignation.

But that was rejected by the club on Friday, with the club saying the 48-year-old's decision stemmed from the "intense emotional impact" of the Europa League exit.

Salah said despite the "disappointment" of the defeat by Ferencvaros, he believed Trabzonspor "will deliver".

"Nothing in my career ever came easy. Bad nights and disappointments are part of football, and I have learned to turn them into motivation and into trophies," he wrote on X.

Sunderland and Bournemouth draw AC Milan in Europa League

"Trabzonspor is my club, and I am part of this project, body and soul. Last night will not change that.

"I know expectations are high, and I truly believe we can and will deliver. 'I came here to win' is not just a slogan to me."

Trabzonspor will instead compete in the Europa Conference League this season, with Scottish side Hearts among their six opponents.

The seven-time Turkish champions have been busy in the transfer market this summer, signing Premier League winners Salah and Fabinho. Andre Onana has also rejoined the club on loan from Manchester United.

Salah, 34, made the shock decision to sign for Trabzonspor last month after mutually agreeing to end his contract at Liverpool last season.

The Egypt international is the third-highest scorer in the Reds' history, behind only Ian Rush and Roger Hunt, after scoring 257 goals in 442 appearances following his move from Roma in 2017.

Salah scored his first two goals for his new club in Saturday's 2-1 win against Istanbul Basaksehir.

articles.title: Luís Castro: "Estamos preparados ante cualquier salida"
articles.standfirst: El entrenador luso ha mostrado tranquilidad ante los posibles movimientos que se puedan producir en los últimos días de mercado
articles.summary: El entrenador luso ha mostrado tranquilidad ante los posibles movimientos que se puedan producir en los últimos días de mercado
articles.body: El Levante se estrena este sábado, a las 17:00 horas, en el Ciutat de Valencia recibiendo al Real Betis en la tercera jornada de liga. El técnico portugués ha afirmado que, "cualquier jugador de la plantilla puede salir y estamos preparados para ello". Así mismo, ha calificado que este fin de semana recibirán a uno de los mejores equipos del campeonato, tanto a nivel individual como colectiva" Margen de mejora del equipo "Siempre hay margen de mejora. Durante la temporada habrá partidos que estarás bien y, siempre hay margen para mejorar, y también como todos los equipos habrá momentos que puedes estar muy bien y puedes perder. Del tiempo que estamos de entrenamientos, estamos a buen nivel de conceptos. Están haciendo las cosas bien y la pretemporada ha sido buena. El único mal de la temporada fue contra el Espanyol pero contra Osasuna mostramos nuestra identidad" Jugar en casa "Es bueno volver a casa. Es donde el año pasado hicimos cosas muy difíciles. Jugar con nuestros aficionados nos dio un punto más. Esto nos da mucha fuerza y muchas ganas" Claves contra el Real Betis "El Real Betis es uno de los mejores equipos de la liga, tanto a nivel individual y colectivo. Tener el mismo entrenador desde hace años, eso es bueno porque los conceptos están alineados con los jugadores y, para ganar a un equipo como este tenemos que estar al 100%" Posibles salidas y entradas "Estamos analizando las posibles salidas y entradas, como todos los equipos. Hasta que no termine el mercado pueden haber movimientos hasta el último día" Problema de las inscripciones "A mí, las inscripciones, no me han hecho daño. Yo trabajo con lo que tengo. Me concentro en soluciones y no en problemas. Si han hecho daño a algunas personas, no lo se. Estaba tranquilo porque tenía calidad para jugar un partido" Carlos Álvarez "Todos pueden salir y otros que pueden entrar. El club está preparado en todas las posiciones, porque mañana puede venir con una oferta de un jugador que no lo esperábamos. Hay muchos jugadores que podrían venir en relación a lo que necesitamos" Posición de Dani Requena y Hugo Sotelo "Son jugadores que están mejorando los dos. Es normal que, cuando no llegas al principio de la pretemporada, es normal que necesites tiempo para conocer el club. Pero los dos pueden estar en las posiciones del centro del campo. Sotelo con un poco más de experiencia y puede jugar con un pivote o dos y Requena, también está trabajando muy bien. Está evolucionando muy bien" Tay Abed "Todos los jugadores saben lo que pensamos. Hay jugadores que, si hay una oportunidad para salir, saldrán y otros que se pueden quedar, pero si viene una oferta muy buena, puede salir. Todos saben lo que pensamos de cada uno" Enfermería "Alex Primo está recuperándose de lo que tenía y los otros, están todos disponibles"

articles.summary: El técnico valora el sorteo de Europa League para el Celta
articles.body: Claudio Giráldez realizó una primera valoración del sorteo de la fase de grupos para los célticos en Europa League: “Sabíamos que iba a ser difícil. Creo que el nivel es muy alto, con equipos emergentes y con equipos históricos y de ligas muy competitivas. Ahora esperaremos para ver cuál es la ruta exacta. Tres equipos que el año pasado jugaban Champions, tres que jugaron previa de esa competición, hace que sea un calendario complicado pero creo que estamos preparados para ello”. Competición ilusionante: “Tenemos ganas de que empiece, creo que es una competición que ilusiona mucho a todos y va a ser muy importante empezarla bien. Estamos muy ilusionados con las tres competiciones para nosotros es un año muy bonito”. Ya tienen la experiencia de la pasada temporada: “Es un aval muy importante para nosotros. Tenemos muy claros los errores que hemos cometido y también las cosas que hemos hecho bien y ese bagaje tenemos que aprovecharlo para ser más estables en la competición. Ojalá podamos hacer un mejor papel, sabemos que es muy complicado, muy difícil, llegar a 1/4 de final como hicimos el año pasado. Ojalá podamos comenzar muy bien y que la competición cada vez nos vaya ilusionando más”. Un encuentro que le apetece especialmente jugar ”El partido ante el Celtic me ilusiona, es un campo con un ambiente espectacular. Todos los partidos de casa también nos motivan en Europa y Bournemouth o Juventus son encuentros muy bonitos. Tenemos partidos muy exigentes en Balaídos, que la gente nos empuje y ayude para poder sacarlos. Luego indagar en equipos menos conocidos pero que están ahí por haber hecho bien las cosas”.

articles.title: Celtic face Benfica in Europa League & Hearts meet Mo Salah's Trabzonspor
articles.summary: Celtic will meet Benfica and Marseille in the Europa League while Hearts will take on Mo Salah's Trabzonspor and Monaco in the Conference League.
articles.body:
Celtic will meet Benfica and Marseille in the Europa League while Hearts will take on Mo Salah's Trabzonspor and Monaco in the Conference League.

Scottish Premiership champions Celtic, who fell into the Europa League after surrendering a four-goal lead against LASK in the Champions League play-off tie earlier this week, will also play Celta Vigo, Besiktas, Omonia, Union SG and Torreense.

Hearts, who lost in Champions and Europa League qualifying but defeated Rapid Vienna on penalties in the Conference League play-off, have fixtures with Borac, Nordsjaelland, Pafos and Thun.

Celtic play their first Europa League fixture next month, with Hearts starting their league phase campaign in October.

"When you have a draw like this, you know you're going to play some really nice games against really good sides," said Hearts head coach Wouter Vrancken.

"You play Europe, so we will put everything in it. It's always nice to play there, so we'll see."

Manager Martin O'Neill said Celtic's Europa League fixtures were "something to look for".

"Benfica's performance against Hearts would show you that they are probably a Champions League team. The competition's still very strong.

"Quite a number of teams in this competition could easily take their place in the Champions League."

Marseille (home), Benfica (away), Ferencvaros (home), Union SG (away), Celta Vigo (home), Omonia (away), Bestikas (home), Torreense (away)

Matchdays: 16/17 September, 15 & 22 October, 5 & 26 November, 10 December 2026, 21 & 28 January 2027

Monaco (home), Pafos (away), Borac (home), Trabzonspor (away), Nordsjaelland (home), Thun (away)

Matchdays: 15 & 22 October, 5 & 26 November, 10 & 17 December

Celtic's rekindled rivalries & Hearts up against Salah

Celtic last played Portuguese side Benfica, who beat Hearts twice earlier this season, in two 2012 Champions League group stage matches, drawing at home and losing away, and defeated Ferencvaros home away in 2021 Europa League games.

During manager Martin O'Neill's first spell as boss, Celtic beat Celta Vigo on away goals en route to the 2003 Uefa Cup final

Celtic have never previously played Turkey's Besiktas, French side Marseille, Cypriots Omonia, Taca de Portugal winners Torreense or Belgium's Union SG, who are part-owned by Brighton chairman and Hearts investor Tony Bloom.

Liverpool great Salah joined Turkey's Trabzonspor this summer after 257 goals in 442 appearances. Now, 34, the Egypt international has two goals in three games for Trabzonspor, who will host Hearts.

Vrancken's side also face trips to Cyprus for Pafos and Switzerland for Thun.

Bosnian champions Borac will visit Edinburgh, along with Danes Nordsjaelland and Ligue 1 Monaco.

In the Europa League, each of the 36 teams will play eight different teams, four at home and four away, in the league phase.

The teams who finish in the top eight will automatically qualify for the round of 16, while those who finish between ninth and 24th will face off in a two-legged knockout tie in the play-off round.

Teams who finish 25th and below will be eliminated from the competition and will not be able to drop into any other European competitions.

In the Conference League, the format is slightly different, as all 36 teams play only six games, three at home and three away, in the league phase.

In terms of qualifying for the next round, however, it is the same format as the Europa League, with the top eight progressing to the last 16, while teams who finish between ninth and 24th enter the play-offs.

The knockout rounds for both competitions take place from February, with the Europa League final on 26 May and the Conference League final on 2 June.

articles.title: Manchester United sign Swedish winger Monica Jusu Bah for £400k
articles.summary: Manchester United have confirmed the signing of Sweden winger Monica Jusu Bah from BK Hacken for just under £400,000.
articles.body:
Manchester United have signed Sweden winger Monica Jusu Bah from BK Hacken for just under £400,000.

The 23-year-old joins on a four-year deal and becomes United's third signing before Thursday's Women's Super League transfer window deadline.

Jusu Bah was under contract until 2028 at Swedish club BK Hacken and United sources say they faced competition for her signature.

"It's an unbelievable feeling to join Manchester United," she said.

"There is a real togetherness in the group and you can feel the excitement from everyone for a big season ahead.

"The opportunity to work with Eva Olid is perfect. Everybody knows the quality of her coaching and her ability to support players to reach their highest level.

"I'm ready to keep pushing myself, help the team achieve our ambitions together and create special memories at this incredible club."

She has played in Sweden for her entire career, breaking through at Umea before moving to BK Hacken in 2023.

In May, Jusu Bah helped BK Hacken win the inaugural Women's Europa Cup.

She has made 11 appearances for Sweden and played in all six of their Women's World Cup qualifying matches this year.

It is understood United hope to add at least one more player before next week's deadline.

United have signed defender Andrea Medina from Atletico Madrid and goalkeeper Janina Leitzig from Leicester City.

articles.title: Jim Goodwin: Dundee United manager may miss match at Kilmarnock after hospital stay

articles.body:
Manager Jim Goodwin may not be in the Dundee United dugout for Saturday's Scottish Premiership match at Kilmarnock after taking ill and being admitted to hospital on Thursday.

Assistant Lee Sharp took first-team training at United's St Andrews base on Friday and also assumed pre-match media duties in 44-year-old Goodwin's absence.

"He is OK, I spoke to him last night and I spoke to him again this morning and he was in good spirits," Sharp said on Friday.

"I don't really know much to be honest, I just asked him how he was and he just said they took him in yesterday and he felt unwell and they are keeping him in for observation."

Dundee United have one point after three Premiership matches while Saturday's opponents Killie are yet to register a point this term after two games.

Sharp was asked if he expects to be taking the team at Rugby Park and replied: "I have absolutely no idea, it is playing it by ear at the moment just to see.

"I will catch up with him later on today and see what happens, it is no more than that really, I really don't know."

articles.title: Southampton FC Women: Simon Parker on 'challenging summer'
articles.summary: Southampton Women's head coach Simon Parker reveals that the summer has been "challenging" for the women's set-up at the club.
articles.body:
Women's Super League 2 side Southampton have had their budget cut significantly after a "challenging" summer, according to head coach Simon Parker.

As part of the changes, the women's team will now play the majority of their matches at Eastleigh FC's Silverlake Stadium, instead of at St Mary's Stadium where they had spent the previous four seasons.

With the new campaign starting a week on Sunday, Parker told BBC Radio Solent they are now operating with the smallest budget in the WSL 2, and this has had a significant impact on their strategy for 2026-27.

"The summer has been a bit challenging with a few of the things that have happened," Parker said.

Sources at Southampton deny that these budget cuts are related to the spygate scandal.

Saints' men were removed from the Championship play-offs last season after the club admitted to spying on rival teams and started this season on minus four points.

In 2025-26, Southampton's women were in the mix for promotion to the WSL, ultimately finishing fifth, their highest position in the football pyramid since re-forming as a club nine years ago.

"It was a strong first year last season where the aim was always to try and finish in the top half and finishing fifth in a promotion push for a large part of the season was really promising," Parker added.

"Off the back of last season, the plan was to re-engage with a lot of our key players but we had to pivot and go into a different direction."

Earlier this summer, it was also revealed director of football Marieanne Spacey-Cale would step down, having been instrumental in the rise of the women's team at Southampton.

Over the past few years, Saints have sold a number of their best players and that trend has continued.

Notable departures in recent years include Lucia Kendall who joined Aston Villa in 2025 and Kayla Rendell who signed for Manchester United in the same window.

Goalkeeper Fran Stanton left the club this summer alongside captain Atlanta Primus, Aimee Palmer and Tara Bourne.

Southampton have played all of their home matches at St Mary's Stadium since winning promotion to the second tier in 2022.

This change in ground will see them move from the 30,000-plus capacity arena to National League side Eastleigh's ground, which can hold just over five thousand fans.

Despite the downsize in grounds, Parker is looking at the positives and new opportunities that the move will bring.

"One of the ideas is they want to try and generate a tighter atmosphere," he added.

"When you play in a smaller stadium that can help with that, I do believe also that if you are playing in the main stadium truthfully, it does cost a lot of money.

"I would love for us to be playing at St Mary's every single week and I love it when we're there, we still have at least three games there this season.

"The definitive reasons (for the move) are not conversations that I'm part of."

Southampton begin their WSL 2 season at Durham on Sunday, 6 September (12:00 BST).

articles.title: Celtic: Northern Ireland's Casey Howe relishing 'surreal' spell in Glasgow
articles.summary: From Maguiresbridge to Celtic, Casey Howe has already packed plenty into a career that has taken her across the UK and Ireland - but her latest chapter may be the most exciting yet.
articles.body:
From Maguiresbridge to Celtic, Casey Howe has already packed plenty into a career that has taken her across the UK and Ireland - but her latest chapter may be the most exciting yet.

A Northern Ireland debut at 17, a treble-winning season with Glentoran, a move to Nottingham Forest and promotion with Wolves have all helped shape the County Fermanagh native, who is now testing herself at one of the biggest clubs in Scottish women's football.

The 23-year-old got off the mark for Celtic on just her second appearance for the club last Sunday, with a beautiful left-footed curler that finally broke the deadlock in the 82nd minute of an eventual 3-0 win over Montrose in the Scottish Women's Premier League (SWPL).

"Being just a young girl from Maguiresbridge, it is pretty surreal to do this," Howe told BBC Sport NI.

The road to the state-of-the-art training centre at Barrowfield in the East End of Glasgow was one paved with long journeys, family sacrifice and a belief that one day she could reach the highest level.

Her parents drove her to Ballinamallard, Cookstown and Belfast four or five days a week as the fleet-footed forward progressed through the ranks.

"They wanted to give me the best platform to be the best I can," she said.

"They were massive in enabling me to take these opportunities and get these opportunities because if it wasn't for them sacrificing a lot of driving, a lot of miles, I wouldn't be here."

Northern Ireland winger Howe joins Celtic after Forest exit

Those sacrifices helped Howe progress at home before opportunities abroad began to emerge.

Following spells with Linfield, Glentoran and Sligo Rovers, a prolific period at Athlone Town in the League of Ireland Women's Premier Division caught the eye across the water.

Now, at Celtic, she believes she has found the environment to take her game to another level.

"I think as a player, you're always looking to develop in any training session.

"It's definitely a big improvement tactically, and we're adapting to different styles, getting used to how Grant Scott (Celtic head coach) wants us to play, so we're always adapting tactically and keeping on top of the technical stuff."

Celtic's attacking approach is particularly appealing to Howe, with the 14-cap international relishing the chance to express herself in the final third.

"We're trying to play a nice attacking brand of football, and as an attacker myself, that's the way you want to play and want to be a part of, is when you're attacking and playing free-flowing football.

"I think that's when you get the best out of people, is when you have that freedom to go forward and make different runs, make different movements, and dribble and drive at people so it's definitely perfect for the way I like to play."

It's an approach that Howe believes brings the best out of her.

"I've played under people in the past where it's almost robotic. You have to do this movement, that movement, but to have the freedom to be allowed to run into different areas or make different movements, it just makes for an all-round performance, team-wise, because everyone's moving.

"It makes it difficult to play against, so it definitely gives you confidence as a player.

"I think you're being backed to do that, and you're being allowed to do that. It definitely gives you confidence."

'I want to leave NI shirt in better place'

The connection to home runs deep, and Howe knows first-hand the challenges young footballers from her own county and elsewhere in Northern Ireland can face in trying to make their way in the game.

"I think sometimes it's hard because being from Fermanagh you don't necessarily have the facilities on your doorstep," she explained.

"A lot of the time, a lot of girls, even young girls now, will still have to travel up and down."

The long drives were familiar to Howe and her family, but she believes every mile is worth it when it leads to success.

"All the sacrifices, as we spoke about earlier, like, winning makes it all worth it."

Her development at Celtic could also have benefits for Northern Ireland.

Howe's ambitions extend beyond what she can achieve at club level, with a desire to help build on the progress made by the national team since she first pulled on the green jersey.

"I want to leave the Northern Ireland shirt in a better place than when I came in.

"I always want that legacy to continue to build and grow."

That sense of responsibility extends to the next generation, with Howe keen to show young girls back home that a career in football is possible.

"If I can leave women's football in Northern Ireland, in Scotland, in England that 1% better than when I joined it - that's a win for me and if that inspires young girls in Fermanagh to push on and know that there is a path there then that's good enough for me," she said.

From the drives out of Fermanagh in pursuit of football to making her mark at Celtic, Howe has already come a long way from her days at Ballinamallard United.

But with trophies to chase, a Northern Ireland legacy to build and young girls back home watching on, there is still plenty of road left to travel.

articles.title: Álvaro Morata, nuevo jugador del Leganés
articles.standfirst: El conjunto pepinero ha hecho oficial la llegada como cedido del delantero español procedente del Como 1907
articles.summary: El conjunto pepinero ha hecho oficial la llegada como cedido del delantero español procedente del Como 1907
articles.body: El CD Leganés ha hecho oficial la llegada de Álvaro Morata en calidad de cedido desde el Como 1907 hasta final de temporada, con una opción de compra al término de la misma. El delantero madrileño se convierte así en uno de los grandes bombazos del mercado de verano en España y, especialmente, en LaLiga Hypermotion. A sus 33 años, Morata aterriza en Butarque con el objetivo de recuperar protagonismo y convertirse en una de las grandes referencias ofensivas del conjunto pepinero en el ansiado regreso a Primera. Su última temporada en Italia no ha sido especialmente prolífica de cara a puerta. Morata disputó 26 encuentros de Serie A con el Como y fue titular en nueve de ellos, sin conseguir marcar en el campeonato liguero y con una asistencia en su cuenta. En la Coppa Italia sí logró estrenarse como goleador, antes de poner rumbo ahora a España para afrontar un nuevo desafío. El fichaje supone un importante salto de calidad y experiencia para un Leganés que quiere pelear por regresar a Primera división. Morata conoce perfectamente el fútbol español, ha jugado en algunos de sus clubes más importantes y llega a Segunda con la vitola de ser uno de los nombres más mediáticos de la competición. Su llegada convierte al Leganés en uno de los grandes protagonistas del mercado y añade un atractivo enorme a LaLiga Hypermotion. Ahora queda por ver si el delantero es capaz de recuperar en Butarque la versión goleadora que le llevó a ser uno de los atacantes más importantes del fútbol español y europeo. Formado en la cantera del Atlético de Madrid y posteriormente en la del Real Madrid, Morata desarrolló buena parte de su carrera en la élite europea. Con el conjunto blanco llegó a debutar con el primer equipo y, tras una primera etapa en Madrid, pasó por la Juventus, el Chelsea, el Atlético de Madrid, el Milan, el Galatasaray y, finalmente, el Como. Una trayectoria a la que hay que sumar más de 80 partidos con la selección española y el título de campeón de Europa conquistado en 2024.

articles.title: Celtic: Martin O'Neill still hopeful over transfers, despite Champions League loss
articles.summary: Celtic manager Martin O'Neill hopes missing out on the Champions League will not mean missing out on prospective targets.
articles.body:
Manager Martin O'Neill hopes missing out on the Champions League will not mean Celtic miss out on prospective signings.

O'Neill's side will feature in the Europa League after Tuesday's 5-1 defeat by LASK after extra time, with the Austrian side winning the Champions League play-off 5-4 on aggregate.

The Scottish Premiership holders have signed four players so far this window, which closes next week.

"I'm hoping that's not the case," O'Neill said, when asked about the possibility of missing out on players.

"We're still trying to get some players in, we would need a few in obviously to supplement the squad.

"I'm hoping that we can get some people in before the transfer deadline."

Visit our Celtic page for all the latest news, analysis and fan views

Celtic have faced criticism from supporters since last summer for the business done - or lack of it - in advance of the Champions League play-offs, which they also lost last season against Kairat Almaty.

Kasper Hogh, Camilo Duran, Haissem Hassan and Mika Baur all arrived at Parkhead before the LASK tie, but influential players Daizen Maeda and Arne Engels left for Ipswich Town and West Ham United, respectively.

"The Champions League is a big carrot for, particularly a lot of younger players," O'Neill said.

"The prestige is not there the same [in the Europa League], it's still a great competition. Obviously, the finance is still the big thing."

Reflecting on "the major disappointment" of Tuesday's loss, O'Neill admitted Celtic "should've been out of sight by half-time", at which stage they led 4-1 on aggregate.

"We did not do well in the second half," O'Neill explained

"The result's the most important thing and we got beaten. I'm obviously disappointed with myself. I have to really analyse it again.

"We could've maybe defended our box a wee bit better. I have to look at my own part before I look at anybody else's.

"You have to recover pretty quickly. You really have to. We have to show real character."

articles.title: Rangers count consequences of European failure - financially & with coefficient
articles.summary: A bruising loss in the Czech Republic gives Rangers pause on various fronts as European football eludes Derek McInnes.
articles.body:
After Jablonec's Jan Chramosta converted from the penalty spot to confirm Rangers' European exit on Thursday, the immediate reaction from the away end was one of understandable anger.

Manager Derek McInnes said he was "embarrassed" and "disappointed" by both the performance and the result as his difficult start at Ibrox continued.

Just one shot on target in 120 minutes against a team they were firm favourites to beat, multiples changes of shape and a multitude of signings failing to have an impact.

But what exactly are the consequences of Rangers missing out on European football this season, both on and off the pitch?

What is financial cost of no European football?

One of the main benefits of playing European competitions is the financial boost it provides.

Rangers finishing third in the Scottish Premiership last season meant they did not have the opportunity to qualify for the Champions League and they were knocked out of Europa League qualifying by Polish side Jagiellonia Bialystok in a further blow.

However, they still had the chance to reach the Conference League - admittedly, the least prestigious and least lucrative of Uefa's three club competitions.

Teams that qualify for the league phase of the Conference League receive about £2.72m, with about £343,000 more for every win at that stage. There is a further £114,000 for a league-phase draw.

There are then exponential rewards for reaching the knockout stages and each win from there on.

Last season's Conference League winners Crystal Palace received at least £15m from the competition, plus the bonus of qualifying for this season's Europa League.

There is also the knock-on effect of fewer matchdays and therefore fewer tickets sold, as well as hospitality and corporate packages.

It remains to be seen if Rangers' summer spending spree will be curtailed by defeat in the Czech Republic.

The Ibrox outfit continue to be linked with a big-money move for Portland Timbers striker Kevin Kelsy, as they try to replace the injured Youssef Chermiti up front.

Another winger also appears to be a priority, with talks reportedly ongoing with Brighton for Amario Cozier-Duberry.

Daisuke Yokota and Kim Min-su have already arrived to join wide players Ross McCausland, Findlay Curtis and Djeidi Gassama.

Might influential midfielder Nicolas Raskin - who did not travel to Jablonec - be sold to fund more new players?

What is clear, Rangers in their current guise do not look capable of challenging for silverware this term.

"When you look at the performance, it is nowhere near good enough, but not a result I didn't expect," former Hibernian and Celtic midfielder Scott Allan said on the BBC's Scottish Football Podcast .

"He literally said himself the team doesn't know what it is. And ultimately that falls on Derek McInnes and what they're doing on the training pitch.

"He talked about elite preparation - the performance was anything but that. If we're totally honest, they're devoid of quality.

"Rangers weren't playing against a top side. That's a game, with what Rangers have spent, they should be coming through quite comfortably."

Podcast: From European agony to weekend Premiership pressure

One saving grace might be fewer games helping sharpen Rangers' focus in domestic competitions.

Title favourites Celtic will have to navigate at least eight matches in the Europa League, while Hearts - who also finished above Rangers last season - succeeded where Rangers failed and reached the Conference League proper, where they have at least six games.

'Bleak picture' for Scotland's coefficient

It's a bleak picture for Scotland and its Uefa coefficient.

After being ranked as high as ninth between 2021 and 2023, at the end of last season Scotland had plummeted to 18th.

This is important because it determines how many places a league gets in Europe each season - and in which competitions.

For instance, last season's placings in the Scottish Premiership earned five places in Europe. For this season going into next, it's down to four.

Scotland is now down to one place in the Champions League, starting in the early rounds.

To get places back, Scotland needs to get back into the top 15. But this week's disastrous results mean there's no chance of that.

Celtic being knocked out of the Champions League and going into the Europa League did not really matter, as it's easier to get results in the secondary competition.

But three of the other teams being knocked out of Europe means there's only a small chance of climbing up the coefficient table.

Historically, Scotland has relied upon the Old Firm for its European results. So Rangers being eliminated is a huge blow.

Now, Hearts will have to step up and make it deep into the Conference League, results in which are worth far fewer coefficient points.

Scotland has already dropped to 19th in the live standings but would need to drop to 34th for the current allocation to be impacted. That cannot happen.

But the gap to 15th is considerable and Scotland would need their best ever season to bridge it.

The good news is, at the end of this season, the 2022-23 season drops off the five-year calculation. And that was one of Scotland's worst seasons.

But if teams continue to fail in the qualifying rounds, Scotland will struggle to reclaim places in Europe.

articles.title: Valverde se centra
articles.standfirst: Mou lo ve principalmente en el eje y el jugador responde mejorando su rendimiento defensivo y con acciones como la del 1-0 ante la Real
articles.summary: Mou lo ve principalmente en el eje y el jugador responde mejorando su rendimiento defensivo y con acciones como la del 1-0 ante la Real
articles.body: Federico Valverde está siendo una de las notas positivas del arranque del Real Madrid en la nueva temporada. La ausencia de Aurélien Tchouaméni, baja en los dos primeros partidos por problemas musculares, ha abierto de par en par las puertas del once para el capitán, al que José Mourinho prioriza en posiciones centradas. Lejos parecen quedar ahora los tiempos de Fede como jugador de banda, cuando llegó a actuar en las tres posiciones del costado derecho, incluidas las de extremo y lateral. Para Mou, Valverde es un jugador de pasillo central, la posición en la que cree que puede aportar más al equipo. Ante la Real, decorchó el partido con una poderosa arrancada casi desde campo propio antes de asistir a Kylian Mbappé en la jugada del 1-0. Pero, más allá de eso, Mou y su staff valoran la capacidad de trabajo del charrúa, considerada clave para mantener el equilibrio de un equipo que juega con prácticamente cuatro jugadores de ataque, a la espera de la entrada de Yan Diomande en los onces titulares. Ante la Real, Valverde firmó tres acciones defensivas, dos recuperaciones y una intercepción, además de ganar dos de tres duelos y no ser regateado en los 90 minutos jugados. Además, acreditó un 93% de acierto en el pase, una cifra notable, con dos pases largos completados sobre tres intentados. A la asistencia a Mbappé sumó dos tiros a puerta, uno bloqueado por la zaga realista y el otro parado por Remiro. El nuevo hábitat pensado por Mourinho para Valverde se circunscribirá, salvo situación de necesidad, al eje del terreno de juego. El entrenador considera que tiene muchas y buenas opciones por banda derecha: Güler, Diomande, Brahim, incluso Bernardo... Jugadores todos ellos que ofrecen garantías, las mismas que el entrenador del Madrid ve e una posición más centrada de Valverde. La baja de Tchouaméni ha permitido a Fede arrancar el curso como intocable. La nueva temporada ha echado tierra sobre el enfrentamiento entre ambos en la recta final del curso anterior, fruto de la gran tensión interna en el vestuario a causa de los malos resultados. De momento, Fede parte con ventaja con respecto al francés. Su rendimiento, sobre todo en defensa, satisface al técnico, que además valora su liderazgo, intensidad y fortaleza física. Y también por una combatividad que el técnico considera esencial a la hora de elevar el nivel general de energía del equipo.

articles.title: Judge Will Hear Recantation of Sexual Abuse Claim Against Ex-Penn State Coach Jerry Sandusky
articles.summary: A judge has granted a hearing to explore claims that a man wants to recant allegations of sexual abuse years ago by Penn State assistant football coach Jerry Sandusky.
articles.body:
A judge has granted a hearing to explore claims that a man wants to recant allegations of sexual abuse years ago by Penn State assistant football coach Jerry Sandusky.

Sandusky, 82, has been serving a decades-long prison sentence since he was convicted of 45 counts of sexual abuse in 2012. Eight young men testified about what happened to them as boys. He has repeatedly lost efforts to get a new trial, but Sandusky's lawyers are trying again.

A man identified in court documents as R.R. said he was coached extensively by authorities.

"I was told — both directly and indirectly — that trauma may have fragmented my memory, and that I could safely affirm details I did not fully recall. I was assured this was common and even expected," R.R. said in an affidavit filed by Sandusky's attorneys.

A court hearing in Centre County has been scheduled for Sept. 8.

R.R.'s allegations were "based on suggestive leading questioning, prosecutorial coercion and influence, confirmatory bias and memory manipulation, which permeated throughout each of the accusers as well," Sandusky's attorneys said in a court filing.

The Pennsylvania Office of Attorney General said Friday that R.R.'s recantation is "highly suspect."

Sandusky coached the defense at one of the country's top football programs under Hall of Fame head coach Joe Paterno. The scandal led to Paterno's firing, and the university paid more than $100 million to people who said they had been abused by Sandusky.

Authorities said Sandusky found and groomed victims at The Second Mile, a charity that he started for at-risk youth. He has repeatedly declared his innocence.

"I apologize that I'm unable to admit remorse for this because it's something that I didn't do," Sandusky said during a 2019 court appearance.

At trial, R.R. was 25 years old. He testified that he was 11 when Sandusky performed oral sex in the coach's basement in 1998, a transcript shows.

"He told me that if I told anybody that I would never see my family again," said R.R., who was in foster care at the time.

Sandusky later apologized and said "he loved me," R.R. testified.

articles.title: No hay 'palos' para Lamine
articles.standfirst: Rozó el gol contra el Athletic, pero Unai y la madera lo impidieron: hay confianza máxima en él
articles.summary: Rozó el gol contra el Athletic, pero Unai y la madera lo impidieron: hay confianza máxima en él
articles.body: Lamine Yamal siempre está bajo los focos. Y su inicio de temporada está siendo, cómo no, escuadriñado. Flick fue el primero en admitir que el internacional aún no está a su mejor nivel, pero la confianza en el extremo catalán es máxima. Nadie, en el club ni en el vestuario, da importancia a que no haya marcado aún, a que le contraríe ser sustituido (mostró su malestar en Elche pero en otros muchos encuentros de otras temporadas también lo hizo) ni cree que esté atravesando un bajón anímico que afecte a su rendimiento. Y para justificarlo, remiten a sus números contra el Athletic. "Tuvo algunos dolores de cabeza... pero es un genio. Tuvo tres semanas de vacaciones y ahora ha trabajado sólo unos días y no pudo estar en Elche a su máximo nivel, hay que intentar que lo recupere pronto. Estoy feliz que jugara 60 minutos y participó en los dos primeros goles en el Martínez Valero. Nos dio opciones para los cambios. Aportó mucho en el partido, y trabaja bien. Avanza. Le necesitamos. Es increíble", dijo Flick tras el primer cruce de la temporada. Y la mejoría ya se vio contra el Athletic. Fue titular en la banda derecha y en esta ocasión disputó los 90 minutos. No vio puerta, pero fue desequilibrante. Como siempre. No bajó los brazos en su ambición de marcar o de ayudar al equipo con sus regates, velocidad, centros... Firmó siete disparos, tres entre los tres palos; creó cinco ocasiones dio 45 pases acertados, completó tres regates, intervino en 85 acciones... El de Rocafonda supo salir de la presión de los defensas del bloque vasco, encaró, lo probó por dentro y por fuera y rozó el gol en varios disparos. Hizo que Unai Simón, elegido MVP del partido, se luciera en la primera mitad, con dos intervenciones de gran mérito, y el palo impidió su primer tanto en la segunda. En el club catalán están seguros de que Lamine brillará también este curso 26-27 porque ya lo está haciendo. No hay preocupación. Hay máxima confianza y tranquilidad.

El Bayern de Múnich y el Stuttgart disputan su primer encuentro de la temporada en la Bundesliga, en un duelo que supone una de las grandes citas de esta jornada inaugural del campeonato alemán. El conjunto bávaro comienza una nueva temporada con el objetivo de volver a imponer su dominio en Alemania y arrancar la Bundesliga con una victoria ante su afición. Por su parte, el Stuttgart llega dispuesto a poner las cosas difíciles a uno de los grandes favoritos al título y a comenzar el curso dando la sorpresa ante el gigante alemán. Será, por tanto, el primer partido de Liga para ambos equipos, un estreno que siempre viene acompañado de ilusión, expectativas y muchas incógnitas después del verano. El Bayern buscará empezar con buen pie su camino hacia el título, mientras que el Stuttgart tratará de demostrar desde la primera jornada que puede competir contra cualquiera. articles.title: El malaguismo se moviliza para el Bernabéu: tres aficionados por cada entrada
articles.standfirst: El Málaga recibió más de 1.800 peticiones para localidades visitantes y muchos seguidores buscan ahora una entrada por su cuenta
articles.summary: El Málaga recibió más de 1.800 peticiones para localidades visitantes y muchos seguidores buscan ahora una entrada por su cuenta
articles.body: El regreso del Málaga a los grandes escenarios del fútbol español no entiende de distancias, precios ni de la escasez de entradas. Este domingo, el conjunto blanquiazul vuelve a uno de los templos del fútbol mundial y la respuesta de su afición ha estado a la altura de la cita. Más de 1.800 malaguistas solicitaron una de las 600 localidades que el Real Madrid puso a disposición del club para la zona visitante. Tres aficionados por cada entrada. El Málaga tuvo que recurrir al sorteo para decidir quiénes serían los privilegiados que podrán ocupar el sector visitante del Santiago Bernabéu. Una representación oficial que será reducida ante la enorme demanda generada por un partido que el malaguismo llevaba años esperando. Después de la multitudinaria presencia blanquiazul en el Metropolitano, Madrid volverá a teñirse de azul y blanco. Y conseguir una entrada tampoco era precisamente una ganga. Las localidades para los aficionados del Málaga tenían un precio de 70 euros y estaban ubicadas en la zona más alta del estadio, el conocido como 'gallinero'. Una cantidad importante para unas localidades alejadas del césped, pero insuficiente para frenar las ganas de estar presentes en una tarde señalada en rojo. El precio tampoco baja demasiado para quienes intenten acceder al Bernabéu por otra vía. El Real Madrid estableció en 75 euros el precio mínimo de las entradas para el público general, mientras que el coste aumenta en función de la zona del estadio. En las plataformas de compraventa, además, el importe puede dispararse. Por eso, el sorteo del Málaga no ha puesto punto final a la carrera por una entrada. Muchos malaguistas siguen buscando una localidad por su cuenta para acompañar al equipo en su regreso al Bernabéu. Redes sociales, grupos de aficionados y plataformas de compraventa echan humo en las horas previas al partido. Los 600 elegidos serán los que oficialmente representen al Málaga en la zona visitante, pero todo apunta a que la presencia blanquiazul en el Bernabéu irá mucho más allá de ese sector. Ocho años después, el Málaga regresa a uno de los escenarios más imponentes del fútbol español. Y el malaguismo no parece dispuesto a perdérselo.

articles.summary: "Sus cualidades de liderazgo y su filosofía de entrenamiento nos entusiasman", aseguró el director deportivo
articles.body: Arturo Ruiz ha sido nombrado nuevo entrenador del primer equipo femenino del Brighton. El ex técnico de la Real Sociedad ha firmado un contrato hasta 2029 y se incorporará al club una vez que se ultimen los trámites de su permiso de trabajo. Zoe Johnson, directora general de fútbol femenino, declaró: "Estamos encantados de dar la bienvenida a Arturo al club. Destacó rápidamente durante nuestro proceso de selección. Cuenta con una trayectoria demostrada en el desarrollo tanto de equipos como de jugadoras. Confiamos en su capacidad para seguir impulsando a este equipo y contará con todo nuestro apoyo mientras ultimamos los preparativos para el inicio de la nueva temporada de la WSL". El director deportivo, Mike Cave, añadió: "Arturo es un entrenador joven y con talento que ha demostrado su capacidad para mejorar los equipos y a las jugadoras con los que ha trabajado a lo largo de su carrera. Sus cualidades de liderazgo y su filosofía de entrenamiento nos entusiasman, y estamos deseando ver lo que puede lograr en nuestro entorno". Tras su etapa en el Granada, Arturo Ruiz se incorporó a la Real Sociedad Femenina en la Liga F. En la temporada 2025-2026, registró un balance de 21 victorias, seis empates y cinco derrotas, asegurando la tercera posición y la clasificación para la fase previa de la UEFA Women’s Champions League.

articles.title: These Group of Six teams have the best shot at making the College Football Playoff in 2026
articles.summary: Will Boise State's move to a rebuilt Pac-12 help its playoff hopes? Can American favorite Navy make the CFP for the first time?
articles.body:
It's highly, highly unlikely that we're going to see two non-power conference champions in the College Football Playoff again.

Thanks to yet another rule change ahead of the third version of the 12-team playoff, the champions of the ACC, Big 12, Big Ten and SEC are now guaranteed a spot in the field. That means the scenario that unfolded last year, where American champion Tulane and Sun Belt champ James Madison both got in since they were ahead of ACC champion Duke in the final CFP rankings, won't happen again.

This year, the fifth conference champion guaranteed into the field will come from either the American, Conference USA, MAC, Mountain West, Pac-12 or Sun Belt. The only way those conferences will send more than one team to the playoff is if a team from the Group of Six gets in as an at-large.

It's why we're resigned to just one Group of Six team in the playoff this December. And we think that team will come from this group below.

After making the College Football Playoff during the 2024 season, the Broncos' playoff dreams basically disappeared in Week 1 a season ago with a 34-7 loss at USF. Boise State then lost by 21 to Notre Dame in Week 5 and a two-game losing streak ended any hope the Broncos had of making back-to-back playoff appearances.

Now Boise State is in the remodeled Pac-12 and a Week 1 loss shouldn't end its playoff hopes this season. Boise State travels to Oregon for the second time in three seasons. In 2024, the Broncos lost 37-34 as both teams ended up in the playoff.

Both QB Maddux Madsen and RB Dylan Riley return and the schedule features other sneaky good non-conference opponents in Memphis and Western Michigan. The defense will need to improve after allowing nearly five yards a carry in 2025 and only accruing 27 sacks after 55 in 2024.

Like Boise State, Fresno State moves from the Mountain West to the Pac-12 and opens against a Big Ten opponent that used to be in the Pac-12. But things are especially more manageable after that Week 1 trip to USC, and the Bulldogs have the benefit of hosting Boise State on Oct. 10 before a potential rematch in the Pac-12 title game.

QB Khristian Martin arrives from Maryland after last season's starter E.J. Warner threw 13 TDs and 11 interceptions. Though the passing game took a major step back in 2025, the offense stayed afloat by a renewed run game and Fresno State's top three backs all return. The defense is full of players who started their careers at power conference schools and allowed just 19 points per game in 2025.

This team hardly resembles the one that made the playoff season ago. Coach Bob Chesney is at UCLA. RB Wayne Knight followed him there. QB Alonza Barnett is at UCF. The top three receivers from last year are no longer on the roster and LB Gannon Weathersby is the only player among the top seven tacklers to return.

Yet there's still reason to believe that JMU is among the Sun Belt favorites and can be in the mix for the CFP. Former Florida coach Billy Napier takes over for Chesney and don't let his Florida tenure make you forget what he did at Louisiana. The Ragin' Cajuns went 33-5 over his final three seasons.

The schedule includes Conference USA favorite Liberty and a trip to San Diego State in Week 3 along with a November visit to a UConn team that was very good in 2025. Yes, there aren't any power conference teams on the schedule. But that could ultimately play into JMU's favor if no one else separates themselves from the Group of Six field.

The Midshipmen are the favorites in the American at +375 despite the departure of QB Blake Horvath after he rushed for 16 TDs and threw for 12 others in 2025.

His replacement is Braxton Woodson, who averaged 9.4 yards a carry on 44 attempts last season and saw time when Horvath was injured. Woodson could easily top 1,000 yards rushing behind an offensive line that returns four starters and paved the way for 286 rushing yards a game in 2025.

The defense brings back its top three tacklers, including LB MarcAnthony Parker. It will need to be better against the pass; Navy's opponents completed 64% of their throws for 230 yards a game last year.

Even if Navy wins the American, avoiding a blowout against Notre Dame may be the key to the Midshipmen's playoff hopes. Since a 35-32 loss in 2022, Notre Dame has won the last three meetings between the schools by a combined 142-27.

Thanks to the multiple defections to the Pac-12, the Mountain West isn't what it once was. But perennial FCS power North Dakota State joins from the second tier and will not be a pushover for the holdovers in the conference.

The Lobos bring back six starters on each side of the ball and won their last six regular-season games in 2025 before an overtime loss to Minnesota in the Rate Bowl. QB Jack Layne threw for nearly 2,500 yards and seven of his 10 interceptions came across two games.

LB Jaxton Eck, the son of coach Jason Eck, led the team with 129 tackles and is one of the best defensive players in the Mountain West. The odds aren't incredibly high, but if New Mexico doesn't get handled by Oklahoma in Week 3, an 11-1 campaign could be enough for a playoff berth and an incredible turnaround from a 2-10 season in 2022.

Like JMU, Tulane follows its playoff appearance up with a new coach as Jon Sumrall is now at Florida. Former Southern Miss coach Will Hall was promoted to replace Sumrall as the Green Wave look for a fifth consecutive season with at least nine wins.

Former Houston and Louisiana QB Zeon Chriss-Gremillion was named the starter after he was Conner Weigman's backup with the Cougars in 2025. RB Jamauri McClure is back after averaging over six yards a carry along with WR Anthony Brown-Stephens.

The defense returns safety Jack Tchienchou and linebacker Chris Rodgers but the pass rush basically needs to be rebuilt from scratch. We'll have an idea of just how playoff-worthy Tulane will be early in the season too. Three of the Green Wave's first five games are trips to Duke, Kansas State and Army. Multiple losses in that stretch may end Tulane's playoff hopes.

What can Dan Mullen do in his second season in Las Vegas? The Rebels went 10-4 in 2025 as QB Anthony Colandrea scored 32 total touchdowns. He parlayed that season into a starting role at Nebraska, so Mullen added former Oklahoma and Auburn quarterback Jackson Arnold through the transfer portal.

Arnold had an up-and-down career in the SEC but could thrive in the Mountain West. RB Jai'Den Thomas rushed for 985 yards and 12 TDs in 2025 and also added 36 catches. He should be one of the most productive backs in the conference yet again.

The defense will have a lot of new faces for the second straight season and needs to be better if UNLV is to have any hope of a season good enough for the playoff. The Rebels allowed 28 points per game in 2025 and 6.4 yards a play.

This is a great chance for the Roadrunners to get back to where they were in 2021 and 2022 when they posted 25 wins across those two seasons. UTSA has gone 7-6 in each of the past two seasons with a defense that has allowed over 28 points per game.

That unit will look a lot different in 2026 while the offense returns QB Owen McCown and RB Will Henderson. McCown threw for 30 TDs and nearly 3,000 yards in 2025 and completed almost 68% of his passes.

A game at Texas in Week 3 is a certain loss, but UTSA gets both Navy and USF at home before a trip to Tulane on Oct. 24. This is a team well-positioned to compete for the American title and, in turn, a spot in the playoff.

articles.title: Farke on Gruev, transfers and 'unstoppable bulldozer' Brentford
articles.summary: Leeds United boss Daniel Farke has been speaking to the media before Sunday's Premier League game against Brentford at Elland Road (kick-off 14:00 BST).  Far...
articles.body:
Leeds United boss Daniel Farke has been speaking to the media before Sunday's Premier League game against Brentford at Elland Road (kick-off 14:00 BST).

Here are the key lines from his news conference:

On the injuries in the squad, Farke said: "It's [Ilia] Gruev's second week training with the team so he's edging closer and closer. Also some good news was Gudmundsson and Gnonto - as it stands they will join us this afternoon [in training] for the first time after their injuries. We have to wait to see how their bodies reacts. Obviously, we just have two days but definitely good news."

On the likelihood of Gruev playing on Sunday, he said: "He has missed more or less four months without playing a game so we have to make a decision. Physically, he is edging closer and closer. He also looks good on the training pitch. If I need him, I would have no problems to call him to the squad. We have now, thank god, a situation where we don't have to rush Ilia."

On the club's transfer window so far, he said: "We are in a good position. Very pleased with our window so far. We will stay aware because the feeling is that we want to do something more. We're definitely in a good place. I like our window so far and all our signings are spot on. Early signs are great but we have a long season."

On the goalkeeping situation, he confirmed Lucas Perri is nearing a loan exit, which was reported earlier on this page, with Leeds set to bring in Michael Zetterer from Eintracht Frankfurt. Farke said: "It's correct that we have allowed Lucas Perri to travel and it's correct that we're pretty close to bringing someone in, but I only want to speak about this once it has been confirmed."

The Leeds boss also said he was "cautiously optimistic" of further new arrivals before the transfer window closes next Tuesday.

On the options for the number nine role, Farke said Dominic Calvert-Lewin and Lukas Nmecha have a "pretty similar" profile but on his options he said he is "happy with this".

Farke described Sunday's opponents Brentford as the "standout" team of the season and "an unstoppable bulldozer". He added that his side will have to be at their very best to get three points.

articles.title: Carrick on Baleba, Amad's injury and JJ Gabriel
articles.summary: Manchester United boss Michael Carrick has been speaking to the media before Sunday's Premier League game against Ipswich at Old Trafford (kick-off 16:30 BST...
articles.body:
Manchester United boss Michael Carrick has been speaking to the media before Sunday's Premier League game against Ipswich at Old Trafford (kick-off 16:30 BST).

You can hit play above, listen on BBC Sounds or take in the key lines from his news conference:

Carrick confirmed that Diallo is still unavailable for selection. Mason Mount is back training with the group.

He spoke highly of new signing Carlos Baleba: "We're delighted with Carlos. [He has] massive potential. I think it's a really exciting signing for us. I think the quality that he has, the attributes that he has, that offsets a little bit of the balance of the group that we've got."

Baleba has a "little ankle issue," which rules him out of action for a few weeks. "It's no major issue," Carrick added.

Both Baleba and Amad could be available before next month's international break but Carrick was reluctant to put a deadline on their return.

When asked about the plan for highly-rated academy player JJ Gabriel: "JJ is one of the boys. He's obviously got a really big talent. He's trained with us quite a bit. He's getting experience all the time. He's physically adapting to each step that he makes, and just continuing his development."

On fellow academy player Harry Amass, whose future at Old Trafford is uncertain: "I've been really pleased with Harry. I think he had a really good season that didn't finish so good with the injury, but it's been great to have him around pre-season. He's done really well. So, let's see what happens."

On Sunday's match: "The first home game of the season is really one we look forward to, and the supporters coming. I think we had a setback last week, and you want to get back to playing well and winning football matches. It is a tough game, Ipswich obviously had a big result last week as well. It'll be another challenge for us."

articles.title: Patrick Nuamah, más polivalencia para el Sabadell
articles.standfirst: El joven y versátil jugador llega a la Nova Creu Alta cedido por el Sassuolo italiano
articles.summary: El joven y versátil jugador llega a la Nova Creu Alta cedido por el Sassuolo italiano
articles.body: Juventud y versatilidad son las dos cualidades que definen a la decimotercera incorporación del Sabadell para la temporada del regreso a LaLiga Hypermotion. Se trata de Patrick Nuamah: un jugador de 20 años que es un caso paradigmático de la polivalencia que tanto aman Ferran Costa y Lucas Viale, el técnico y el director deportivo del club arlequinado. Nuamah resulta difícil de ubicar en una posición fija sobre el césped. Puede actuar en las bandas y también en ataque. Debutó en la Serie B a los 16 años con la camiseta del Brescia y ya suma más de 50 partidos en la categoría de plata del fútbol italiano. También ha sido internacional con las selecciones transalpinas sub18, sub20 y sub21. Con este currículum llega a la Nova Creu Alta en calidad de cedido. Desde Italia aseguran que el Sabadell se guardaría una opción de compra por valor de un millón y medio por esta joven promesa. El comunicado de la entidad catalana le define como "un jugador con una gran proyección" que destaca "por su potencia física, su versatilidad sobre el campo y su capacidad de aportar trabajo, sacrificio y polivalencia". El verano pasado cambió el Brescia por el Sassuolo con un contrato de cinco años y luego salió cedido al Catanzaro. Jugó un total de 29 partidos con el equipo entrenado por Alberto Aquilani e incluso disputó la promoción de ascenso a la Serie A. Este verano ha realizado la pretemporada con el Sassuolo y el domingo vivió desde el banquillo la derrota en casa del Atalanta. Ahora ha dado un nuevo paso en su carrera de la mano del Sabadell y de Ferran Costa, un enamorado de la polivalencia. En su aún corta carrera Nuamah ha jugado de centrocampista ofensivo y defensivo, interior y extremo por las dos bandas e incluso como segundo delantero y delantero centro.
